# SocialTap for Python

SocialTap is the social media scraper API for developers and AI agents. Send a public link, a handle or a search and get live data back in one schema. Failed requests are free.

The Python SDK for the SocialTap API: a method for every endpoint, typed models and errors, retries and pagination.
Generated from the SocialTap catalog (version 1.600.37). Docs: https://socialtap.dev/docs/. Source: https://github.com/SocialTapDev/socialtap-python.

## Install

Not published to PyPI yet: install it from source, from GitHub.

```sh
pip install "git+https://github.com/SocialTapDev/socialtap-python"
```

Zero dependencies (the standard library's urllib); Python 3.10+; fully typed (`py.typed`, checked with `mypy --strict`).
Models are frozen dataclasses with the API's field names; `None` means unknown, lists are never `None`.

Nothing is invented: a required member that is missing or of the wrong type raises `APIDecodeError`, as does a
2xx that is not the API's envelope; with `fields=` the data is a `dict` of the selected members (typed overloads). Every
result keeps `raw` (the decoded body), members this version doesn't model included. A `retry-after` longer than
`MAX_RETRY_AFTER_S` raises `RetryAfterExceededError` instead of retrying early. `Event.data` is the model of its type;
job items are TypedDicts per endpoint.

Async: `AsyncSocialTap` has the same methods as coroutines (`async for` over `iterate`). It runs the stdlib
transport in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread`), which is plenty for API calls that take about a second; pass
`transport=` (anything with `send(Request) -> Response`) to bring another HTTP stack.

```python
import asyncio
from socialtap import AsyncSocialTap

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncSocialTap()
    res = await client.tiktok.profile.get(handle="nasa")
    print(res.data)

asyncio.run(main())
```

## Authenticate

The client reads your API key from `SOCIALTAP_API_KEY`, or takes it as an option. Requests send it in the
`x-api-key` header. Get a key at https://socialtap.dev/signup/: every account starts with 100 free credits.

## First call

TikTok Profile API (`tiktok.profile`). Exact follower and like counts, bio and country.

```python
from socialtap import SocialTap

client = SocialTap()  # api_key defaults to os.environ["SOCIALTAP_API_KEY"]

res = client.tiktok.profile.get(handle="nasa")
print(res.data)
print(res.credits.charged, res.meta.request_id)
```

Every result also carries the envelope `meta` (request ID, source, cache status, fetch time) and `credits`
(charged by this request, and the balance after it when the API reports it). Failed requests and cache hits are free.

### Endpoints newer than this package

A version has a method for every endpoint the API had when it was released. For a newer one, update the
package, or send the request yourself: the raw request adds your key and retries and raises errors like a method,
and returns the status, headers and body (the envelope, `data` and `meta`). Each endpoint's docs page has its path
and params.

```python
r, body = client.request("GET", "/v1/tiktok/profile", query={"handle": "nasa"})
print(r.status, body["data"])
```

## Errors

Every API error is an `APIError` subclass named after its code, with `status`, `code`, `retryable`, `remediation`,
`request_id` and `credits_charged` (0: errors are free). Codes this SDK version doesn't know arrive as a plain
`APIError` with their `code`; no response at all is an `APIConnectionError` (`APITimeoutError` for timeouts).

```python
from socialtap import APIError, NotFoundError

try:
    client.tiktok.profile.get(handle="nasa")
except NotFoundError:
    ...  # Check the link or ID. Do not retry.
except APIError as err:
    print(err.code, err.status, err.retryable, err.remediation, err.request_id)
```

| code | class | status | retried |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invalid_input` | `InvalidInputError` | 400 | no |
| `invalid_cursor` | `InvalidCursorError` | 400 | no |
| `unauthorized` | `UnauthorizedError` | 401 | no |
| `forbidden` | `ForbiddenError` | 403 | no |
| `insufficient_credits` | `InsufficientCreditsError` | 402 | no |
| `spend_limit_reached` | `SpendLimitReachedError` | 402 | no |
| `rate_limited` | `RateLimitedError` | 429 | yes |
| `request_too_large` | `RequestTooLargeError` | 413 | no |
| `method_not_allowed` | `MethodNotAllowedError` | 405 | no |
| `endpoint_retired` | `EndpointRetiredError` | 410 | no |
| `idempotency_key_reused` | `IdempotencyKeyReusedError` | 422 | no |
| `idempotency_key_in_progress` | `IdempotencyKeyInProgressError` | 409 | yes |
| `job_not_found` | `JobNotFoundError` | 404 | no |
| `unknown_endpoint` | `UnknownEndpointError` | 404 | no |
| `not_found` | `NotFoundError` | 404 | no |
| `private_or_unavailable` | `PrivateOrUnavailableError` | 403 | no |
| `no_transcript` | `NoTranscriptError` | 404 | no |
| `no_live` | `NoLiveError` | 404 | no |
| `no_media` | `NoMediaError` | 404 | no |
| `no_readme` | `NoReadmeError` | 404 | no |
| `unavailable_for_legal_reasons` | `UnavailableForLegalReasonsError` | 451 | no |
| `upstream_blocked` | `UpstreamBlockedError` | 503 | yes |
| `upstream_error` | `UpstreamError` | 502 | yes |
| `overloaded` | `OverloadedError` | 503 | yes |
| `internal` | `InternalError` | 500 | yes |

## Retries and timeouts

Retryable failures (the codes above, connection errors, timeouts) are retried 2 times by default with
exponential backoff and jitter, honoring `retry-after`. A GET retry sends `max_age` set to the seconds since the first
attempt: if the first response was lost in transit, the retry is served free from the cache. Timeouts are per
attempt: 60 s by default, and 300 s for endpoints that may transcribe audio (`facebook.ad_transcript`, `facebook.transcript`, `instagram.transcript`, `kick.transcript`, `linkedin.transcript`, `reddit.transcript`, `rumble.transcript`, `tiktok.transcript`, `twitch.transcript`, `x.transcript`, `youtube.transcript`), because speech-to-text on long
media takes minutes, and for create-and-wait's long-polls. Most requests answer in a few seconds. A timeout you set, on the client or on one request,
applies to every endpoint, and so does `maxRetries`.

## Pagination

List endpoints return one page (`data`, `page.has_more`, `page.next_cursor`). `iterate()` returns a `Paginator` (`for` over items, `.by_page()` for pages; `async for` on
the async client) with two guards, `max_pages` and `max_credits`; afterwards `pages_fetched`, `credits_charged`, `stop_reason` (`"end"`, or the
guard that stopped it) and `end_reason` (the API's `page.end_reason`) say what happened.
Each page is checked against its catalog price before it is fetched, and an empty page with `has_more` is not the end.

```python
items = client.amazon.deal_products.iterate(max_pages=10, max_credits=100)
for item in items:
    print(item)
print(items.pages_fetched, items.credits_charged, items.stop_reason, items.end_reason)
```

## Account, API keys, jobs, webhooks and events

The gateway's own routes (account, usage, credit ledger, API keys, jobs, webhook endpoints, events) are free and
have methods too, named from their operation IDs (`<noun>.<verb>`, or `<noun>.<sub>.<verb>` for a sub-resource). They
answer the same envelope (`data`, `meta`, `credits`) with their own `meta`; cursor-paged list routes have `iterate` like
list endpoints. Every POST sends an `idempotency-key` header (yours, or a new UUID kept for the call's retries), so it is
retried like a GET and a retry never repeats the work; `replayed` says when the API answered from an earlier request
with the same key, and `status` is 202 when accepted work continues. Each route needs a key with the scope below (a key
never gets a scope its creator lacks).

```python
res = client.account.get()
print(res.data, res.meta.request_id)
```

|---|---|---|
| `account.get` | `client.account.get()` | `account:read` |

### Jobs and webhooks

Many requests (or one long list walk) run as a background job at the synchronous prices; failed items are
free. The create-and-wait helper creates one, long-polls it until it ends and returns every result; one Idempotency-Key
covers the create's retries, so a retry never runs a job twice. Webhook deliveries are signed per Standard Webhooks:
verify the raw body with your endpoint's secret before trusting it, and deduplicate on the event ID.

```python
out = client.jobs.create_and_wait(requests=[{"custom_id": "row-1", "endpoint": "tiktok.profile", "params": {"handle": "nasa"}}])
for r in out.results:
    print(r.custom_id, r.status, r.error.code if r.error else None)

# A webhook delivery: the raw body, the request headers, your endpoint's secret.
event = client.webhooks.verify(raw_body, request.headers, os.environ["SOCIALTAP_WEBHOOK_SECRET"])
```

## Tools for AI agents

The SDK hands the SocialTap MCP server's tools to a model: each tool's name, description (its price
and rules included) and input JSON Schema, and a call that sends one stateless MCP request with your key. A tool
behaves exactly as it does for an MCP client: concise results (`detail: "full"` for every field), `next_cursor` to
continue, and failures returned as the tool's output (`error` with `retryable` and `remediation`) so the model can
act on them. Transport failures raise as for any request, and tools that may be repeated are retried.

```python
# LangChain: pip install "socialtap[langchain]"; the default tools, or SocialTapToolkit(tools=[...] or "all").
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from socialtap.langchain import SocialTapToolkit

agent = create_agent(model, tools=SocialTapToolkit().get_tools())  # any LangChain chat model

# Any other tool-calling API: hand TOOLS (name, description, input_schema) to the model, run its calls with call_tool.
from socialtap import SocialTap
from socialtap.tools import TOOLS, call_tool

r = call_tool(SocialTap(), "find_endpoint", {"query": "TikTok profile"})  # acall_tool with AsyncSocialTap
print(r.is_error, r.output)
```

## Versioning

The version is derived from the API contract: major = API version, minor = the contract's revision (it grows
with every additive change, a new endpoint included), patch = the SDK generator's revision. Questions and bug reports: support@socialtap.dev.
